later.

div.div:
Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents runs the managed Codex harness with an OpenAI model on Amazon
Bedrock. It chooses candidate dimensions, compares measured results and retains context across
review rounds. The default model is GPT-6.1 Sol.

an immutable job ID in S3. The agent supplies design parameters; the deployed broker fixes the
worker, command document and storage destination.

div.div:
On one EC2 instance, a trusted supervisor runs the FreeCAD author, freezes its output files, and
starts a separate FreeCAD checker. The checker runs 11 checks on the frozen candidate. Rows a–c in
the EC2 rectangle show these sequential stages.

div.div:
The supervisor publishes the native CAD files, check report and accepted or failed verdict to
private, encrypted, versioned S3. Recorded versions and SHA-256 hashes bind the evidence to the
files that were checked. This is row d in the EC2 rectangle.

div.div:
BMA retrieves the receipts and recommends a candidate against the latest brief. The client
verifies the downloaded evidence and produces JSON and Markdown reports for the engineer. A later
round can reuse an existing checked design while EC2 is stopped. The result remains
awaiting_review for the engineer's decision.

div.div:
An existing BMA exec-server on AgentCore Runtime can provide planning scripts, reusable skills and
working files. Persistent session storage supports retaining those files when configured. This
integration requires separate provisioning and has not been live-validated.

div.div: Stop EC2 at the scheduled deadline

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 950px; height: 1px; padding-top: 2323px; margin-left: 1209px;

div.div:
EventBridge Scheduler independently calls StopInstances at a configured UTC time for cost control.
It can interrupt a running CAD job. Stopping EC2 preserves the BMA session, EBS disk and S3
evidence; retained storage remains billable.
